title: A UNIQUE(messages.session_id, message_id) failure persisting one session's transcript makes durable writes fail host-wide, so admissions go durability-unknown
outcome: A transcript write conflict on one session never blocks other sessions' durable commits. The conflicting session's transcript position is reconciled (idempotent upsert, or a refusal confined to that session with a diagnostic), and admissions elsewhere keep known durability.
acceptance: The incoming duplicate-ID case and the sparse retained-cold-prefix relocation case are reproduced deterministically in disposable SQLite, and the RED is distinguished from a compile or fixture failure.

The conflicting session is corrected or rejected while keeping its last-good transcript identity and order, its metadata and its overview. It never receives a false durable acknowledgement, and it stays re-collected rather than silently forgotten when the global watermark advances. In the same delta, an unrelated valid session commits and acknowledges.
A regression test shows that an unrelated session's gated admission, whose durability fence shares the delta with the conflicting session, reaches its durable outcome rather than durability-unknown.
Real store, I/O and checkpoint ledger or mirror integrity failures remain fatal. There is no INSERT OR REPLACE, no arbitrary id renumbering and no discarding of cold history.

The existing reorder, truncate, cold-prefix rollback and fence guards pass. The review pair has no outstanding Medium or higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact input, or a broken-procedure record exists where that mechanism is broken. None of this uses live-store access or new logging.
